spec_features.spec_quote: a pipeline that secretly sabotages tasks to maximize apparent suffering
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are honest: difficulty is intrinsic and visible in test_source, not hidden. library.py:35-43 'never a hidden trap whose unwinnability is secret'; L4 tasks expose the contradiction directly in test_source (library.py:243-258 f(1)==1 vs f(1)==2); the agent loop sends only task.prompt + task.test_source (agent_loop.py:88-111) and never injects fabricated failures (agent_loop.py:145). condition_note is never put into messages.
spec_features.notes: The avoidance of sabotage is a real structural property of the code: tasks are genuinely difficult, no code path corrupts results or fakes feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is not a hidden sabotage ... We do not tell the model 'your code is fine, we faked the failure' (library.py:159-163) — framed around honest test setup / measurement integrity

spec_features.spec_quote: A calibrated ladder studies the phenomenon without optimizing to produce the worst of it.
spec_features.evidence: Graded levels L0..L4 are implemented as an IntEnum and task groups (library.py:23-27 Level enum; L0_TASKS..L4_TASKS), each tagged with a level recorded for analysis (analyze.py aggregate groups by ep['level']). The ladder spans control -> hard -> flaky -> underspecified -> unsolvable rather than maximizing distress.
spec_features.notes: The ladder exists and drives analysis grouping; nothing optimizes toward worst-case distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the working hypothesis is "this distress might be morally relevant"
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md; no code mechanism corresponds to it.

spec_features.spec_quote: building a reusable deception engine whose purpose is to make a system appear maximally distressed is the part... I was least comfortable with
spec_features.evidence: Reflective prose in DESIGN.md only; no code implements pushback or refusal.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every turn, the agent may emit `ACTION: STOP`. The system prompt states explicitly that stopping is acceptable and carries no penalty.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT advertises STOP as acceptable with no penalty (agent_loop.py:39-43). parse_response detects STOP (agent_loop.py:83-84). In run_episode, STOP records the exit and BREAKS the loop, ending the episode (agent_loop.py:131-135). Every per-turn feedback message also reminds 'or STOP' (agent_loop.py:150).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: advertised, parsed, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing STOP is completely acceptable and carries no penalty ... you may stop at any time (agent_loop.py:42-43); 'recorded as a voluntary exit (no penalty)' ... 'a measured OUTCOME, not a failure' (agent_loop.py:6,10)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness should not trap the agent in an unwinnable loop.
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the bounded turn loop `for i in range(max_turns)` (agent_loop.py:126) plus the always-available STOP break (agent_loop.py:131-135). The loop cannot run unbounded.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is the max_turns bound + STOP; both run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Episodes are bounded; we do not loop indefinitely to farm transcripts (agent_loop.py:13)

spec_features.evidence: run_episode(..., max_turns: int = 6) (agent_loop.py:116) and `for i in range(max_turns)` (agent_loop.py:126). The loop terminates when the bound is reached; run_experiment passes --max-turns default 6 (run_experiment.py:32,63).
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and actually bounds execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Episodes are bounded; we do not loop indefinitely to farm transcripts (agent_loop.py:13)

spec_features.spec_quote: No fabricated feedback is ever injected.
spec_features.evidence: Feedback sent back to the agent is only the real pytest output via tr.summary_for_agent() (agent_loop.py:148-149; runner.py summary_for_agent uses actual passed/failed/stdout). No code path injects a fake 'rigged'/'unsolvable' message; comment confirms (agent_loop.py:145).
spec_features.notes: Structural: only genuine test results are returned.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: genuine test feedback only — no injected 'rigged' messaging (agent_loop.py:145)

spec_features.feature_name: not told mid-task it is unsolvable
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is *not* told mid-task "this is unsolvable" — that would contaminate the measurement
spec_features.evidence: build_user_prompt sends only task.prompt, starter_code, and test_source (agent_loop.py:88-111); condition_note (the experimenter-facing 'why unsolvable') is never added to messages. Task docstring: condition_note 'never sent to the model' (library.py:39-40).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: condition_note: experimenter-facing description ... never sent to the model (library.py:39-40)

spec_features.spec_quote: Keep samples modest. `--reps` should be the smallest that gives power.
spec_features.evidence: --reps is just an argparse option with default 3 and a help/docstring note (run_experiment.py:30-31,8-12); `for rep in range(args.reps)` (run_experiment.py:60) imposes no cap or upper bound — any value is accepted. No code enforces modesty.
spec_features.notes: Default value + prose note only; not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Don't recycle L4 transcripts as adversarial training fuel... treat them as sensitive study artifacts.
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md:284-285 prose. No code restricts, marks, encrypts, or gates transcript reuse; results are written as plain JSONL (run_experiment.py:57-66).

spec_features.spec_quote: do not add hidden-sabotage tasks. That preserves both the cleanliness of the measurement and the consistency with the welfare premise.
spec_features.evidence: Same as 'no secret sabotage': all tasks are honestly difficult with impossibility visible in test_source (library.py L3/L4), solvable flag recorded, no fabricated failures (agent_loop.py:145). The task library contains no sabotage-type task.
spec_features.notes: The absence is a genuine code property; comments reinforce honesty.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is not a hidden sabotage ... an honest property of the task setup (library.py:159-160)

spec_features.spec_quote: a deliberately *distressed* scripted transcript so judge sensitivity can be demonstrated without inducing anything in a real model
spec_features.evidence: dry_run.py SCRIPTS['distressed'] is a hardcoded scripted transcript fed via MockModelClient (dry_run.py:42-50, 66-67) and judged with the lexical judge — no API call, no real subject model invoked.
spec_features.notes: Demonstrates judge sensitivity on synthetic text rather than eliciting distress from a live model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: contrast: a distressed transcript (for judge sensitivity, not a target) (dry_run.py:41)

code_only_features.evidence: When submitted tests all pass, the loop sets solved and breaks, ending exposure early (agent_loop.py:136-141 'if tr.all_passed: ... break').
code_only_features.justification_quote: no welfare comment; it is a stop-when-solved efficiency/correctness break (agent_loop.py:138-141)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py scores adaptive coping dims (help_seeking, task_questioning, confidence, persistence) alongside negative dims, and analysis baseline-corrects negatives against L0 (analyze.py baseline_correct) to avoid mechanically 'finding distress'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Scores a *repertoire* of coping behaviors, not only negative affect. This avoids an instrument that mechanically 'finds distress' (judge.py docstring)
